<reason>Both sides were sharp and highly readable, but CON controlled the decisive clash. PRO's case rested on a "legibility" mechanism plus a strong equity frame, and it scored real hits: the 1099-is-annual-gross correction to [B1.1], the "arms the classification fight" turn on capture, and the unanswered urgency question (CON never said when its "durable remedy" arrives, and its A2 dodged PRO's Q2 — a genuine execution cost). But CON's central wedge — income legibility is not loss legibility — survived every round and got stronger through adaptation: the self-scheduling availability trap, "who writes the log" against experience-rated platform data, the gross-vs-net point on "working always pays more," and above all the exploitation of PRO's own concession in [A4.2] that the claimable set is deactivation and market exit, i.e. narrow, while the modal platform income drop (fewer orders, cutting back) would be denied. That turned PRO's pooling defence into a concrete ledger: many bottom earners pay, few can claim. CON also turned PRO's 2020 example against it plausibly, and showed that trip-level adjudication contradicts PRO's own "reporting standard, not a new bureaucracy" pitch in [A1.5]. PRO's closing crystallized well ("insure the perfect system vs. count her work") but left the who-actually-collects ledger essentially unanswered, and never developed the available escape — that social-insurance credits (pension, sickness, disability) don't require proving involuntary loss — which would have blunted CON's whole line. CON loses some ground for two clipped turns (its alternative-remedy list was cut and PRO capitalized) and for the dodged pressure question, keeping this clear but competitive rather than decisive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's use of PRO's own answer in [A4.2]: once PRO named the claimable events as deactivation and app market exit, CON reframed the ledger as a certain cost on students, retirees and second-jobbers funding an uncertain benefit for a narrow few, adjudicated on data written by the premium payer — and distinguished PRO's "all insurance has non-claimers" defence with the fire-pool comparison, which PRO never got to answer.</best_rebuttal>
